overall: The AG found violations for untimely approval of two 2020 sets of minutes and for failing to answer a complaint within 14 business days, declined to audit 67 sets of minutes, and ordered future compliance.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to timely approve and provide 67 sets of minutes for meetings held from 2016 to 2020.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review whether all 67 sets of meeting minutes have been timely approved as our office will not conduct broad audits of public bodies based on generalized allegations.

allegations.summary: Failure to timely approve minutes of 2020 meetings that were not posted to the town website (June 29 and December 9, 2020).
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board failed to timely approve minutes of the June 29, 2020, and December 9, 2020, meetings, as the minutes were not approved within the later of the next three meetings or 30 days following each meeting.

allegations.summary: Second complaint alleged the Board failed to timely respond to the first Open Meeting Law complaint, which was overlooked for about six months.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board failed to respond to an Open Meeting Law complaint within 14 business days, we find that it violated the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements to create and approve minutes in a timely manner and to respond to complaints within the required timeframe.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
